target: For every nonnegative integer n and every nonempty compact E⊆ℝⁿ, with I=[0,1] and E×I equipped with the metric induced by concatenated Euclidean coordinates, dim_H(E×I)=dim_H(E)+1.

obstacle_assessment.reasoning: The reported defect is a correctable direction-of-inclusion error, not a substantive gap. For each t∈I, the indices with t∈B_i already cover E, since every (x,t) lies in some V_i. Because B_i⊆J_i, the indices with t∈J_i also cover E. Thus the pointwise content inequality follows; integrating its measurable right-hand side does not require B_i to be measurable.

complete_proof:
For A in a metric space let c_a(A,δ) be the infimum of Σ_j diam(W_j)^a over countable covers by sets of diameter at most δ. Hausdorff measure is, up to a fixed positive normalization, the limit of these contents as δ decreases to zero. We use the threshold properties: H^q(A)=0 if q>dim_H(A), and H^s(A)=∞ if 0≤s<dim_H(A).

Put D=dim_H(E) and F=E×[0,1]. The metric is d((x,t),(y,u))=(|x−y|²+|t−u|²)^(1/2). Since E is compact it is bounded, and a bounded subset of ℝⁿ has finite Hausdorff dimension: for integer m>n, covering a bounded box by O(ℓ^(−n)) cubes of side ℓ gives total m-power diameter cost O(ℓ^(m−n))→0. For n=0 the ambient space is a singleton, so finiteness holds as well.

Upper bound: Fix q>D, so q>0 and H^q(E)=0. At every scale δ>0, E therefore has countable covers by sets of diameters at most δ and arbitrarily small total q-power cost. Discard empty sets. Replace singleton members, if any, by balls of positive diameter at most δ, choosing their q-power costs to have arbitrarily small sum (for the jth replacement, bound the added cost by η2^(−j)). Thus we may take all covering diameters r_j positive and at most δ, with arbitrarily small Σ_j r_j^q. Take δ≤1. Subdivide [0,1] for each j into at most 1/r_j+1 intervals of length at most r_j. The products cover F, and each product has diameter at most √2 r_j by the displayed product metric. Their total (q+1)-power cost is at most Σ_j(1/r_j+1)(√2r_j)^(q+1)≤2(√2)^(q+1)Σ_jr_j^q. Their diameters are at most √2δ. Taking the original q-cost arbitrarily small gives H^(q+1)(F)=0. Hence dim_H(F)≤q+1 for every q>D, and letting q decrease to D gives dim_H(F)≤D+1.

Lower bound if D>0: Fix 0<s<D, so s>0 and H^s(E)=∞. Consequently c_s(E,δ)→∞ as δ↓0. Fix 0<δ≤1 and any countable cover (V_i) of F by sets of diameters ρ_i≤δ; discard empty members. Let A_i and B_i be their projections to ℝⁿ and ℝ. Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz, so diam(A_i), diam(B_i)≤ρ_i. Choose for each i an open interval J_i containing B_i, of length at most ρ_i+η_i, where η_i>0. Choose η_i so Σ_iη_iρ_i^s<ε; for an enumeration indexed by positive integers, η_i=ε2^(−i)/(1+ρ_i^s) suffices.

For each t∈[0,1], the sets A_i for which t∈B_i cover E: for every x∈E, some V_i contains (x,t). Since B_i⊆J_i, the sets A_i for which t∈J_i also cover E. Their diameters are at most δ; hence for every t∈[0,1], c_s(E,δ)≤Σ_i1_{J_i}(t)ρ_i^s. The right side is a measurable nonnegative series, since each J_i is open. Integrating over [0,1] and applying Tonelli for nonnegative series gives c_s(E,δ)≤Σ_i|J_i∩[0,1]|ρ_i^s≤Σ_i(ρ_i+η_i)ρ_i^s≤Σ_iρ_i^(s+1)+ε. Terms with ρ_i=0 contribute zero because s>0. Let ε↓0, then take the infimum over all covers of F at scale δ; this yields c_s(E,δ)≤c_(s+1)(F,δ). Since the left side tends to infinity as δ↓0, so does the right side. Thus H^(s+1)(F)=∞ and dim_H(F)≥s+1. This holds for all 0<s<D; taking their supremum gives dim_H(F)≥D+1.

If D=0, choose x₀∈E, using nonemptiness. The coordinate projection p:F→[0,1], p(x,t)=t, is 1-Lipschitz since |t−u|≤d((x,t),(y,u)), and is onto since p(x₀,t)=t. The Lipschitz dimension inequality and dim_H([0,1])=1 give dim_H(F)≥1=D+1. This includes n=0. Combining the lower and upper bounds proves the claimed equality.

source_obligations.details: Subdivide [0,1] into at most 1/r+1 intervals of length ≤r. For countably many singleton replacements, choose individual positive radii with summable arbitrarily small q-cost.

edge_cases: Nonemptiness is essential under dim_H(∅)=0; the target preserves the nonempty hypothesis.
For D=0, use the onto coordinate projection rather than positive-exponent slicing.
The proof includes n=0, where ℝ⁰ is a singleton.
Zero-diameter cover members are enlarged in the upper bound; in the lower bound they contribute zero since s>0.
Compactness supplies boundedness; the covering argument otherwise needs only boundedness for the ambient dimension bound.
The metric is the concatenated Euclidean metric; no unproved max-product identification is used.
This is a completed natural-language proof candidate, not an NL0 graph, fresh Audit A, or Lean-checked proof.
